title: Visions and Revelations of the Lord
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Context of False Apostles
subpoints: Hyper-apostles claimed superior pedigree and presence
They claimed exclusive visions and revelations
Paul contrasts their paid knowledge with free gospel proclamation

outline.title: The Vision of the Third Heaven
subpoints: Distinction between body and spirit in the vision
Identification of the third heaven as Paradise

outline.title: Inexpressible Words and Divine Restraint
subpoints: Hearing words not lawful for a man to utter
Comparison to John’s experience in Revelation
God’s command to remain silent to prevent pride

outline.title: Boasting in Infirmities
subpoints: Refusal to boast in heavenly experiences
Alignment of weakness with the cross of Christ

summary:
In this afternoon service, Pastor Tito Lyro continues the sermon series on 2 Corinthians by examining Paul’s response to the 'super apostles' who claimed superior spiritual credentials. The sermon highlights the contrast between these false teachers, who withheld knowledge for financial gain, and Paul, who freely proclaimed the gospel to all. Paul addresses the accusation that he lacks visionary authority by referencing his own ecstatic experience of being caught up to the third heaven, or Paradise, fourteen years prior.

The exposition clarifies that while Paul’s experience was real, the specific words he heard were inexpressible and forbidden from being shared to prevent spiritual pride. This divine restraint serves as a counter-cultural witness against modern tendencies to publish heavenly experiences for personal glory. Instead of boasting in such revelations, Paul chooses to boast in his infirmities, emphasizing that the Christian life is characterized not by glory, but by the daily taking up of the cross.

The message concludes by urging believers to align their identity with the weakness of Christ rather than seeking personal elevation through spiritual experiences. True apostolic authority is demonstrated not by exclusive access to divine secrets, but by a humble reliance on God’s grace amidst human frailty.
